summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for her eighth cycle of high-dose methotrexate for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with CNS involvement. She tolerated the chemotherapy well, with no signs of mucositis or infection. Methotrexate was administered at a reduced dose of 3500 mg/m² and followed by leucovorin rescue. Her methotrexate level declined to 0.03, allowing discharge. She remained neutropenic with an ANC of 420 but was afebrile and stable. Diabetes management included holding metformin during admission and increasing the dose upon discharge. Potassium supplementation was initiated due to hypokalemia. Prophylactic ciprofloxacin was prescribed for neutropenia. The patient was discharged home with instructions to continue leucovorin, monitor for infection, and follow up for lab testing and oncology evaluation.
